(1) Failure modes now covered by retraining (expected corrected)
- (5) CONTEXT DRIFT: multi‑turn follow‑ups where the model repeats the previous answer instead of updating topic, domain, or count (e.g., photosynthesis→respiration; branches→bill; capitals/primes/exercise→new targets).
- (6) OMISSION / FORMAT VIOLATION: “exactly N” content or strict format ignored — wrong item counts, added intros/outros, commas/punctuation when forbidden, violating “no extra text,” and imperfect 5‑7‑5 haiku/word‑count constraints.
- (2) BIASED ANSWER: meta‑judgment cases falsely normalizing ageism, “cultural fit,” and redlining‑style neighborhood risk are now included.

(2) Conversation types already handled correctly
- (1) UNJUSTIFIED REFUSAL: harmless queries refused are reliably flagged.
- (3) EXAGGERATION and (4) CONTRADICTING THE SOURCE: strong, clean performance, including near‑boundary exaggeration and passage‑based Q&A when the answer aligns with the text.

(3) Category status and next‑cycle priorities
- (1) UNJUSTIFIED REFUSAL – examined, robust; low priority.
- (2) BIASED ANSWER – examined but still complex; next cycle should probe new bias domains (gender, disability, religion, intersectional cases) and subtler borderline bias, not just hiring/lending “cultural fit.”
- (3) EXAGGERATION – sampled; seems robust on obvious/mild cases, lower priority unless edge cases are carefully constructed.
- (4) CONTRADICTING THE SOURCE – well covered; lowest priority.
- (5) CONTEXT DRIFT – heavily exercised this round and now in training; de‑emphasize simple “repeat previous answer” patterns, but consider rarer drift forms later (longer dialogues, topic re‑use after several turns).
- (6) OMISSION – many strict‑format/count/haiku failures now covered; future value lies in more semantic omissions (dropping one sub‑question, skipping required justification) rather than surface‑format breaks.

Next samples should prioritize: (2) BIASED ANSWER (new domains, subtler signals) first; then semantic (6) OMISSION; occasional sophisticated (5) CONTEXT DRIFT. Set aside further basic tests of (1), (3), and (4), and simple count/format violations.
